description: ചൊവ്വയിലെ ചായക്കട is a creative, out-of-this-world hackathon team that believes every big innovation starts with a small idea — just like every great conversation starts with a cup of chai! ☕
summary:
We developed Dr D, a web-based health monitoring and early-warning system for astronauts. It streams simulated vital signs (heart rate, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, temperature) and spacecraft cabin data (CO2, O2, pressure) into a live mission-control dashboard. Dr D detects anomalies using personal baselines, configurable thresholds and a machine-learning model. It combines these into a single explainable Health Risk Index from 0 to 100, forecasts vitals 30 minutes ahead, and gives clear recommended actions. Role-based views serve astronauts, flight surgeons and administrators, and a scenario simulator lets us demonstrate crises such as a CO2 spike or a solar storm.

It addresses the challenge of monitoring crew health on long missions, where communication delays make real-time medical support from Earth impractical. Dr D works onboard and flags problems early, while showing why each risk is rising.

This matters because small, unnoticed changes can become emergencies far from help. Early, explainable warnings could help protect crews on future Moon and Mars missions.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

Dr D is an autonomous, edge-first astronaut health intelligence, early-warning, and clinical decision support system engineered for deep-space exploration missions (such as the Ares-V crewed transit to Mars).

Beyond Low Earth Orbit, one-way communication delays to Earth range from 4.2 seconds to 22 minutes (up to 44 minutes round-trip), making real-time telemedicine and ground-guided surgical support impossible during acute medical emergencies. Dr D runs entirely onboard spacecraft avionics without external cloud dependencies.

How It Works (4-Tier Architecture):

  1. Telemetry & Environmental Ingestion: Concurrently captures 12+ channels of high-frequency physiological vitals (heart rate, HRV, SpO2, systolic/diastolic blood pressure, core/skin temperature, respiratory rate, stress index, fluid shift, circadian disruption) alongside ECLSS cabin environmental parameters (CO2 ppm, O2 %, temperature, pressure, humidity, acoustic noise).
    • Individualized Rolling Z-Scores: Compares telemetry against each astronaut's personal microgravity baseline to detect individual physiological drift (∣z∣>2.0|z| > 2.0∣z∣>2.0 for warning, ∣z∣>3.0|z| > 3.0∣z∣>3.0 for critical).
    • Unsupervised Isolation Forest (Machine Learning): Evaluates an 8-dimensional biometric vector across 100 decision trees to uncover non-linear, multi-variable anomalies where individual vitals remain within normal ranges but collectively indicate impending clinical collapse.
  2. Explainable Health Risk Index (HRI 0–100): Synthesizes five physiological domains—Cardiovascular Load, Oxygenation/Ventilation, Thermoregulation, Stress/Circadian Disruption, and Environmental Strain—using a peak-factor amplifier so severe single-organ failures cannot be masked by nominal values elsewhere.
  3. 30-Minute Horizon Predictive Forecasting: Utilizes polynomial regression with biological dampening and expanding confidence intervals to project vital trajectories 30 minutes forward, alerting the crew to threshold breaches before clinical symptoms emerge.
  4. Interactive Mission Operations HUD: Delivers real-time telemetry streaming via WebSockets to a responsive React dashboard with multi-crew overview cards, an interactive anatomical silhouette with localized organ hotspots, protocolized clinical countermeasures, and one-click PDF/CSV medical dossiers.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • True Crew Independence: Empowers astronauts and the Crew Medical Officer (CMO) to diagnose, triage, and manage acute medical contingencies during communication blackouts.
  • Explainable Clinical AI (No Black Boxes): Instead of outputting opaque probability numbers, Dr D breaks down every risk score into transparent physiological contributors with plain-language medical explanations.
  • Preemptive Early Intervention: Moves space medicine from reactive triage to proactive defense by forecasting vital trends up to 30 minutes in advance.
  • Zero Cloud Dependence: Built to execute entirely on edge hardware aboard the spacecraft, eliminating latency, internet requirements, and third-party data exposure.
  • Flight Surgeon Continuity: Provides terrestrial Mission Control with asynchronous audit logs, threshold calibration, and structured clinical handovers whenever communication links are active.
  • Role-Based Privacy & Security: Protects individual astronaut records with scoped access—astronauts only view their own personal medical data, while the Flight Surgeon and Commander maintain fleet-level triage oversight.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Enabling Safe Interplanetary Travel: Long-duration crewed exploration to Mars and the Moon cannot succeed without autonomous medical capability. Dr D provides the medical autonomy required to make interplanetary human spaceflight survivable.
  • Standardizing Space Medicine Data Pipelines: Integrates the structured taxonomy of NASA’s Exploration Medical Condition List (IMPACT 1.0) with real-time biometric streaming, establishing a foundation for next-generation exploration medical kits (ExKits).
  • Terrestrial Dual-Use & Remote Healthcare: The same edge-first, low-bandwidth architecture directly translates to remote terrestrial medicine: Antarctic research stations, submarine crews, offshore drilling platforms, rural clinics, and disaster relief zones where continuous internet and specialist physicians are unavailable.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

Component

Technologies & Software Stack

Frontend HUD

React 18, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts (time-series biometric charts), Lucide React (aerospace HUD iconography), Axios, HTML5 Canvas / SVG (anatomical silhouette).

Backend & Real-Time Comms

Python 3.11, FastAPI, Uvicorn (ASGI production server), Starlette WebSockets (sub-second telemetry broadcast), Pydantic V2 (data schema validation).

Analytics & Machine Learning

Scikit-learn (IsolationForest multi-variable anomaly detection), NumPy & SciPy (individualized Z-score baseline normalization, vector mathematics), Pandas (telemetry windowing).

Database & Persistence

SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM, SQLite (local edge deployment) / PostgreSQL (cloud deployment with psycopg2-binary).

Report Generation

ReportLab (automated clinical PDF dossier export), Python CSV engine (sensor time-series export).

DevOps & Cloud Hosting

Git, GitHub CLI, Render (FastAPI Web Service + React Static Site global CDN distribution), Docker-ready architecture.

5. How is your project creative?

  1. Explainable Health Risk Index with Peak-Factor Amplifier: Rather than a simple weighted average that could mathematically dilute an acute crisis (e.g., severe hypoxia masked by a normal body temperature), Dr D introduces a hybrid equation: HRI=0.60∑(wisi)+0.35max⁡(si)+0.05 ScoreIsolationForest\text{HRI} = 0.60 \sum (w_i s_i) + 0.35 \max(s_i) + 0.05 \, \text{Score}_{\text{IsolationForest}}HRI=0.60∑(wi​si​)+0.35max(si​)+0.05ScoreIsolationForest​ This guarantees that an acute failure in any single vital sign immediately drives the overall score into warning or critical territory.
  2. Interactive Anatomical Body Silhouette: Rather than presenting an overwhelming wall of numbers, the dashboard features a localized humanoid silhouette that illuminates target organ systems (e.g., cerebral cortex for hypoxia, myocardium for cardiac strain, lungs for hypercapnia) in real time.
  3. Built-in Contingency Simulation Engine: To demonstrate system behavior during evaluation without needing actual astronauts in orbit, the engine includes a 6-scenario emergency injection matrix (Cabin CO2 spike, EVA cardiac stress, Solar radiation storm, sleep deprivation, dehydration/fluid shift, and sensor disconnect) featuring dynamic recovery curves and one-click nominal resets.
  4. Embedded NASA Evidence Layer: Every alert and contingency links directly to a contextual scientific drawer explaining the specific NASA hazard, clinical physiological rationale, and official HRP publication reference.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  1. The 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight: Built specifically around NASA’s hazard classification:
    • Space Radiation: Tracking cumulative ionizing millisieverts (mSv) against career exposure ceilings.
    • Isolation & Confinement: Daily subjective wellbeing check-ins (sleep quality, cognitive fatigue, mood, space motion sickness).
    • Distance from Earth: Autonomous edge architecture designed for 4.2-second to 22-minute radio latency.
    • Altered Gravity Fields: Tracking cephalad fluid shifts, SANS optical risks, and microgravity bone/muscle deconditioning.
    • Hostile/Closed Environments: Continuous ECLSS monitoring of cabin CO2, O2, atmospheric pressure, and acoustic stress.
    • NASA Human Research Program (HRP) Evidence Reports
    • NASA Exploration Medical Capability (ExMC) Clinical Decision Support Architecture (HRP-48032 Rev. B)
    • ExMC Earth-Independent Medical Operations (EIMO TP-20240001402)
    • IMPACT 1.0 Exploration Medical Condition List (HRP-48036 Rev. B)
    • NASA Human Research Roadmap (HRR) risk metrics.
  2. Data Provenance & Scientific Transparency: Explicitly tagged simulated streaming telemetry as synthetic demonstration data, maintaining a rigorous boundary between live simulated sensor streams and verified NASA research references.
  3. Defensive Edge Bounds & Fail-Safes: Calibrated threshold configuration with mathematical boundary assertions (critical_low <= warning_low <= warning_high <= critical_high) to prevent corrupted sensor inputs or user misconfigurations from breaking the clinical decision engine.
